stem.en: Financial statements of a company are prepared under:

options.en: Schedule I of the Companies Act, 2013
Schedule III of the Companies Act, 2013

explanation.en: Section 129 read with Schedule III of the Companies Act, 2013 prescribes the form of the Balance Sheet and Statement of Profit and Loss.

stem.en: Financial statements are a combination of:

options.en: Recorded facts, accounting conventions and personal judgements

explanation.en: They use recorded (historical) facts, follow accounting conventions and postulates, and involve personal judgements such as the method of depreciation.

stem.en: The two main financial statements of a company are:

options.en: Balance Sheet and Statement of Profit and Loss
Bank Reconciliation Statement and Trial Balance

explanation.en: The Balance Sheet shows financial position on a date; the Statement of Profit and Loss shows performance for a period.

stem.en: Which of the following is NOT an objective of financial statements?

options.en: To provide information about earning capacity
To show the market price of the company’s shares
To provide information about economic resources and obligations

explanation.en: Financial statements report resources, obligations, performance and policies; they do not report the share price on the stock exchange.

stem.en: Calls-in-advance received by a company are shown under:

explanation.en: Calls-in-advance are not yet part of share capital; the company owes interest on them, so they are shown under Other current liabilities.

stem.en: A debit balance of the Statement of Profit and Loss (surplus) is shown in the Balance Sheet:

options.en: As a negative figure under Reserves and surplus

explanation.en: Schedule III requires a debit balance of surplus to be shown as a negative figure under Reserves and surplus, even if the total becomes negative.

stem.en: Bank overdraft is shown under:

options.en: Current assets: Cash and cash equivalents

explanation.en: A bank overdraft is a loan repayable on demand, so it is a short-term borrowing.

stem.en: A company issued 1,00,000 equity shares of ₹10 each, fully called up. Calls-in-arrears are ₹6,000. Subscribed but not fully paid capital is shown at:

explanation.en: Called-up capital ₹10,00,000 less calls-in-arrears ₹6,000 = ₹9,94,000.

stem.en: Which of these is shown under Trade payables?

explanation.en: Trade payables are amounts owed for goods and services bought in the normal course of business: creditors and bills payable.

stem.en: Loose tools are shown in the Balance Sheet under:

explanation.en: Schedule III lists loose tools, along with raw materials, work-in-progress, finished goods and stores and spares, under Inventories.

stem.en: Goodwill is shown under:

explanation.en: Goodwill has no physical form but gives long-term benefit, so it is an intangible asset.

stem.en: A factory building that is still under construction on the Balance Sheet date is shown as:

explanation.en: Assets being constructed and not yet ready for use are shown as Capital work-in-progress.

stem.en: Prepaid insurance is shown under:

options.en: Non-current assets: Long-term loans and advances
Current assets: Cash and cash equivalents

explanation.en: Prepaid expenses are short-term benefits receivable within the operating cycle, shown under Other current assets.

stem.en: When the normal operating cycle of a company cannot be identified, it is assumed to be:

explanation.en: Schedule III states that if the operating cycle is not identifiable it is assumed to be twelve months.

stem.en: Interest on debentures is shown in the Statement of Profit and Loss under:

explanation.en: Interest on borrowings, including debentures, is a finance cost.

stem.en: For a manufacturing company, dividend received on its investments is shown under:

explanation.en: Revenue from operations is income from the main business; dividend on investments is Other income for a non-financial company.

stem.en: Salaries, wages and contribution to provident fund are shown under:

explanation.en: All payments and benefits to employees are grouped as Employee benefits expense.

stem.en: Opening inventory of stock-in-trade is ₹50,000 and closing inventory is ₹80,000. "Changes in inventories" in the Statement of Profit and Loss is:

explanation.en: Change = opening − closing = ₹50,000 − ₹80,000 = −₹30,000. An increase in inventory reduces total expenses.

stem.en: Revenue from operations ₹10,00,000; other income ₹50,000; total expenses ₹7,50,000; tax rate 30%. Profit for the period is:

explanation.en: Total income ₹10,50,000 − expenses ₹7,50,000 = profit before tax ₹3,00,000; tax ₹90,000; profit for the period ₹2,10,000.

stem.en: Which of the following is a limitation of financial statements?

options.en: They show the financial position on a date
They are prepared in a prescribed form
They ignore changes in the price level

explanation.en: Assets are shown at historical cost, so the effect of inflation (price-level changes) is not reflected.

stem.en: Financial statements do NOT reveal:

options.en: The share capital of the company
The quality of management and employee relations

explanation.en: Only items measurable in money are recorded; qualitative factors such as management quality or morale are ignored.

stem.en: Debentureholders and long-term lenders are mainly interested in the company’s:

options.en: Long-term solvency and ability to pay interest

explanation.en: Long-term lenders want assurance that interest will be paid regularly and the principal repaid on time.

stem.en: Presenting financial statements so that the position looks better than it really is is called:

explanation.en: Window dressing is the manipulation of accounts to show a better picture; it is one reason financial statements may mislead.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Calls-in-arrears are deducted from subscribed capital in the note on Share capital.
Reason (R): Calls-in-arrears are the amounts called up by the company but not yet paid by the shareholders.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Both are true; since the called amount has not been received, it is deducted to show the paid-up capital.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Loose tools are shown under Property, plant and equipment.
Reason (R): Under Schedule III, loose tools are part of Inventories.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: A is false because loose tools are shown under Inventories; R is true.

stem.en: Under which sub-head will the bank overdraft be shown?

explanation.en: A bank overdraft is repayable on demand: Current liabilities → Short-term borrowings.

passage.en: Kaveri Ltd. extracted the following balances from its books on 31 March 2025: Trade receivables ₹2,40,000; Bills payable ₹60,000; Bank overdraft ₹1,00,000; Interest accrued on debentures ₹12,000; Stores and spares ₹30,000; 9% Debentures (redeemable in 2030) ₹5,00,000. The accountant has to place each item under the correct head and sub-head of the Balance Sheet as per Schedule III.

stem.en: From the items given, the amount shown under "Other current liabilities" is:

explanation.en: Only interest accrued on debentures (₹12,000) is an other current liability. Bills payable are Trade payables and the overdraft is a Short-term borrowing.

passage.en: Kaveri Ltd. extracted the following balances from its books on 31 March 2025: Trade receivables ₹2,40,000; Bills payable ₹60,000; Bank overdraft ₹1,00,000; Interest accrued on debentures ₹12,000; Stores and spares ₹30,000; 9% Debentures (redeemable in 2030) ₹5,00,000. The accountant has to place each item under the correct head and sub-head of the Balance Sheet as per Schedule III.

stem.en: Under Schedule III of the Companies Act, 2013, 'calls-in-advance' is shown in the Balance Sheet under:

explanation.en: Calls-in-advance is money received before it is called; it is a liability of the company and is shown under 'Other current liabilities'.

stem.en: As per Schedule III, loose tools are shown under the sub-head:

explanation.en: Inventories include raw materials, work-in-progress, finished goods, stock-in-trade, stores and spares, and loose tools.
